newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher despite late pressure.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher despite late pressure.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended higher but drew pressure late from hedge selling and local profit taking, traders said.
Overall, spring wheat gained on a mixture of technical fund buying, commercial short covering and mill buying.
U.S. wheat markets were buoyed early by worries over the extent of rain-related damage to the Argentine crop and by jitters over possible cold damage to U.S. winter wheat.
MGE traders said the rally in wheat prompted some country movement, which ushered in a late round of hedge selling. Locals also were taking profits, they said.

MGE spring wheat closed three to 12-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up 12-1/2 cents at $4.37. March gained 6-1/4 cents to close at $4.00-1/4. Earlier, March had hit an intraday high of $4.06, its highest level since Oct. 16.

Traders said Country Hedging sold three million March bushels on the day, most of it hedge-related. Benson-Quinn and Wilson bought a combined five million March but turned sellers late. CIS and ADM also bought March.
MGE barley futures did not trade and closed unchanged.
